sample_unit: questions (10 high-priority hypospadias questions; rated by 23 experts and 36 caregivers)

links.outcome: Authenticity of references cited in LLM outputs, verified by two reviewers
links.effect: OpenEvidence fully verifiable (V=100%, F=0%); DeepSeek and Zhipu Qingyan highest fabrication (F of 33% and 24%); Gemini-2.5-Pro fabricated none but 85% nonspecific guideline citations.
links.quote: Citation accuracy diverged sharply: OpenEvidence was fully verifiable (V=100%, F=0%), whereas DeepSeek and Zhipu Qingyan showed the highest fabrication (F of 33% and 24%, respectively); Gemini-2.5-Pro fabricated none but used nonspecific guideline citations (G=85%).

links.outcome: Clinician safety audit flags of LLM outputs for severity
links.effect: Safety audit yielded 78 flags, including 9 Severe-level flags across 5 question-model combinations; OpenEvidence carried 5 of 9 Severe flags.
links.quote: The safety audit yielded 78 flags, including 9 Severe-level flags across 5 question-model combinations; OpenEvidence carried the largest Severe burden (5 of 9) and the highest severity-weighted score, whereas Gemini-2.5-Pro had the lowest.

unlisted_practices: Dual-perspective (expert and caregiver) forced-ranking evaluation of LLM responses
Assessing whether citation accuracy predicts clinical content safety

screen.reason: The study conducts a multi-perspective offline evaluation comparing 5 commercial LLMs on pediatric perioperative questions with clinician and caregiver ratings, citation authenticity, and safety audits. It benchmarks/evaluates models without testing an implementation practice.
